member_targets: The specified length (distance measurement) of the baton exchange zone in a standard relay race.

The starting position/mark within or relative to the exchange zone that an outgoing runner should take, as a coaching decision criterion balancing accelerating to speed against the risk of a failed handoff.
The standard length (distance measurement) of the permitted baton exchange zone in relay racing.
The length of the exchange zone — i.e., the distance available within which the baton pass must be completed before the runners exit it.
The physical length (distance measurement) of the regulation baton exchange zone in a standard relay race.
The standard length measurement (distance) of the relay baton exchange zone.
The specific starting distance (a positional threshold ahead of the exchange zone) at which the outgoing runner should begin accelerating.
The physical length/dimension of the standard baton exchange zone in relay racing, expressed as a measurement.
The physical length (distance measurement) of the permitted baton exchange zone.

The method or procedure by which relay teams work out the correct start-mark placement for the outgoing runner (how the distance/position is calculated or established in practice), not merely the fact that start marks are rehearsed.
The physical length (distance measurement) of the permitted baton exchange zone.
The standard length (distance measurement) of the permitted baton exchange zone in relay racing.
The decision procedure or criteria coaches use to select the outgoing runner's starting mark/point for acceleration, balancing speed at handoff against risk of exchange failure outside the zone.
The spatial positioning (relative distance and alignment) the incoming runner should maintain with respect to the outgoing runner at the moment of the baton exchange.
The procedures or adjustment methods teams use to recalibrate start marks for new runner pairings differing in stride length and speed.
The spatial relationship (separation/relative placement) between incoming and outgoing runners at the moment the handoff begins.

The consequence and resulting procedure (e.g., whether the team is disqualified or who may retrieve the baton and how the race continues) when the baton is dropped during a relay exchange — an outcome not addressed by the passage's description of exchange-zone rules and handoff timing.
The standard length (distance measurement) of the relay baton exchange zone.

The decision procedure or criteria a coach should use to set each outgoing runner's start mark within the exchange zone, balancing acceleration gains against the risk of a failed or out-of-zone handoff.
The decision procedure or criteria coaches use to set the outgoing runner's start mark, trading off acceleration benefit against risk of a failed or out-of-zone handoff.

The decision procedure or criteria coaches should use to set each outgoing runner's start mark, balancing acceleration gains against the risk of failing to complete the handoff within the exchange zone.
The method or criteria by which relay teams set the outgoing runner's start mark (its placement/distance), i.e., how that position is calculated or determined.

The method or criteria by which a runner's optimal start mark within the exchange zone is set — i.e., what factors (incoming runner's speed/approach, outgoing runner's acceleration profile, zone length, risk of overrunning or missing the handoff) are used and how they are combined or calibrated to fix that point.
The set of considerations or variables that govern the coaching decision of the outgoing runner's starting point for acceleration, balancing speed gain against exchange-zone risk.
The typical distance run by the outgoing runner between starting acceleration and receiving the baton, expressed as a quantity of distance.
The method or procedure by which the outgoing runner's optimal start mark is established (e.g., how the starting point is calculated or set in practice).

The method or decision procedure coaches use to set each outgoing runner's specific start mark within the exchange zone.

The method or criteria by which relay teams calculate and set the start mark — i.e., the distance ahead of the exchange zone at which the accelerating runner should begin running — based on the two runners' relative speeds and timing.

The method or procedure by which relay teams set the start-mark distance at which a runner begins accelerating ahead of the handoff (how the optimal acceleration-start distance is determined), rather than the fact that such marks are rehearsed.

The decision procedure or criterion coaches use to set each outgoing runner's start mark within the exchange zone, i.e., how the speed benefit of an earlier start is balanced against the risk of a failed or out-of-zone handoff.
The typical distance or lead time by which an outgoing relay runner starts accelerating ahead of the baton exchange (i.e., the start-mark offset), expressed as a quantity.
The method or adjustment procedure by which relay teams calibrate start-mark placement to the specific speed and stride characteristics of each outgoing/incoming runner pairing.
The specific adjustments made to start-mark placement and handoff timing to accommodate a pairing in which the incoming and outgoing runners have markedly different speeds.

The set of pairing-specific variables (e.g., incoming runner's arrival speed and fatigue, outgoing runner's acceleration profile and reaction, zone geometry) that jointly fix where the outgoing runner should place the start mark.
The amount of practice/rehearsal time or number of repetitions a relay team typically requires to achieve reliably smooth baton exchanges

focal_unknown_anchor: The coaching choice is where each outgoing runner should begin moving so that speed gains do not create too much exchange risk.
